source.title: Mean--Fluctuation Dynamics at the Edge of Stability

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own gradient-descent and model-comparison experiments on near-edge-of-stability dynamics, including whether a covariance model tracks gradient-descent behavior and when it fails. This bears conceptually on V5, but does not test the learning-rate recovery/stability claims in that version.
record.gate_note: The paper's experiments compare mean–fluctuation (MF) dynamics and other continuous-time models with saved gradient-descent trajectories; they do not report training classification error, label memorization, local-minimum frequency, or normalization/initialization effects. Rows below capture direct GD-versus-MF covariance/trajectory evidence and the explicitly reported onset comparison. Cited prior-work claims are not rows. MF-versus-Rod or other solver comparisons alone are omitted unless the reported result bears on the claim's object.
record.test_reason: The study's own full-batch GD runs measure training loss and Hessian sharpness, directly bearing on V5's edge-of-stability clause. The record incorrectly excludes these observations because they also serve as references for flow-model comparisons. Full-batch GD with squared loss and sharpness tracking uses the same method and measures as the original edge-of-stability study.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the empirical comparisons. The authors also emphasize a rigorous GD-to-MF approximation under restricted sharp-valley assumptions, stationary-state stability analysis, and a conditional kinetic description for wide two-layer models. Their covariance-model failures are limitations of the approximation, not evidence that GD fails to exhibit edge-of-stability training.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and compares continuous-time mean–fluctuation dynamics against saved full-batch gradient-descent trajectories. Its experiments are on subsets of CIFAR-10 using mean-squared loss and measure loss, sharpness, centers, and covariance, not the classification training-error outcome in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture (MLP, CNN, ResNet), one versus two near-EoS modes, learning rate, seed, initialization at the EoS onset, and comparison horizon affect the reported MF-to-GD accuracy. The paper notes accumulated covariance error in longer runs and deterioration at higher learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: MF approximates GD trajectories with accuracy that depends on architecture, mode count, learning rate and horizon; Rod can fail to grow critical fluctuations at onset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuous-time covariance models reproduce selected finite-time GD dynamics with model-dependent limitations.

record.problems: The experiments use one seed for the main architecture comparisons and small CIFAR-10 subsets. The tracked covariance diagnostics project onto only three leading Hessian directions and explicitly do not measure fluctuations outside that subspace. Some comparisons are limited to short horizons; the authors report accumulated covariance errors in longer runs. The reported measurements concern MF model fidelity, not classification training error.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows were retained. The main experiments in Sections 3 and C.2 compare MF/other flows with GD on loss, sharpness, centers, and covariance; these measures do not establish whether the classification training-error outcomes named by V1–V4 or V6 occur, nor the learning-rate behavior named by V5. The cited prior work and solver-refinement results are not independent findings on the claim.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, random-label memorization, and the effects of model size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher–student networks and its reduction through extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and special recipes for deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for training speed and trainable depth.

Recovery after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit, the catapult loss transient, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite initially subthreshold sharpness. Most reported comparison windows begin at selected EoS checkpoints rather than random initialization.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Direct GD loss and sharpness results were wrongly excluded wholesale in rows_left_out. Extract the seed-cohort GD observations separately from MF/Rod approximation errors: falling window-averaged loss and leading effective eigenvalues near 2 over 4,000 steps, with ten one-mode and nine two-mode completed trajectories.
Extract the GD onset trajectory starting at ηλ1 ≈ 1.999: loss, sharpness and growth of critical variance over 4,000 steps. Keep GD observations separate from Rod's failure and MF's success.

Retain direct GD loss and sharpness traces from the architecture and learning-rate experiments as V5 evidence. Record architecture, rate, onset selection and horizon, and distinguish instantaneous GD sharpness from sharpness evaluated at the GD-window center.
missing.locator: Figures 6, 7, 17 and 24; Sections D.1, D.3 and D.5

record.verdict_notes: No existing rows require correction because the record contains none. Its central eligibility error is treating all reference GD measurements as method-performance evidence. Only the direct GD behavior supports V5; flow fidelity, solver refinement and covariance-closure errors do not warrant limits_scope or challenges labels for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 memorization, corrupted/random labels, model size, optimizer recipes, and early stopping.
Teacher–student two-layer ReLU spurious minima and the effect of extra student width.
Plain versus residual network training error by depth, and special recipes for training deep networks.
Activation-matched, orthogonal, Gaussian, or convolutional initialization comparisons and trainable depth.

The study concerns learning rates near the edge-of-stability and describes the threshold mechanism, but its reported experiments compare model trajectories rather than test recovery from above the initial linearized stability limit, sharpness hovering while loss falls, or divergence rates. No result row measures the behavior V5 names.
Batch normalization speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

relationships.condition: Full-batch MLP training on 8,000 CIFAR-10 images with squared loss, η = 0.002, across the completed seed cohorts.
relationships.reason: Based on text and Figure 22, pending missing rows: GD loss falls over 4,000 steps while leading effective sharpness remains near ηλ = 2; the one-mode cohort contains ten seeds and the two-mode cohort nine.
relationships.display_finding: Loss fell over 4,000 steps while leading effective sharpness stayed near ηλ = 2 across ten one-mode seeds and nine two-mode seeds.

relationships.condition: MLP onset run starting just below the threshold, ηλ1 ≈ 1.999, with η = 0.002.
relationships.reason: Based on Figure 8 and Section C.2, pending missing rows: GD develops critical fluctuations, sharpness oscillates near the threshold, and loss ultimately falls over the 4,000-step window.
relationships.display_finding: Starting at ηλ1 ≈ 1.999, training developed critical fluctuations and near-threshold sharpness oscillations while loss ultimately fell over 4,000 steps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
